title: Latency Callgraph Tileboard: per-model & per-route p50/p95/p99 with IO-mode decomposition
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: build a Tileboard-style dashboard that surfaces latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) broken down by call-graph node, model and route, and by IO mode (streaming vs non-streaming). The board should make it easy for oncall and SRE to: (1) find which model or route is contributing to tail latency, (2) determine whether latency is due to RPC/IO vs CPU-bound token generation, and (3) pivot from metric spikes to traces/segments with pre-populated trace hooks.

Why this is different: existing dashboards are mostly endpoint- or model-centric and show aggregate percentiles. This ticket introduces callgraph decomposition tiles: each tile is a small waterfall-like view that attributes percentiles to serving runtime components (proxy layer, router, kernel execution, KV cache miss, IO waits). We also add explicit IO-mode decomposition (streaming vs non-streaming) side-by-side so teams can quickly see mode-specific regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tileboard displays p50/p95/p99 for selected time window aggregated across customer route, model, and callgraph node names.
- Each tile includes streaming vs non-streaming split and absolute count of sampled requests per bucket.
- Clicking a tile opens a trace search pre-filtered to the offending node, time range, and IO mode (trace hook parameters set).
- Telemetry schema changes are backward-compatible; we provide a translation layer for older traces.
- Dashboard has baseline runbook links and an alert recipe for sudden p99 increases with sampling guidance.

Telemetry & instrumentation plan:
- Trace hook: add a callgraph node tag (serve.node) and io.mode tag (streaming|nonstreaming) emitted by the runtime.
- Metrics: emit histogram/granular latency buckets per node/model/route/io.mode. Use existing metrics channel (OTel exporter -> vector -> clickhouse/metrics store).
- Logs: add a compact latency fingerprint to access logs to ease correlation (fingerprint includes model, route, node, io.mode, request_shard).

Implementation steps:
1) Spike (completed): validated cost of adding node-level latency histograms at 1% sample. Prototype code in runtime spike branch. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
2) Schema design (completed): doc with new tags and translation for older traces. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Callgraph+Tileboard+Schema
3) Metrics pipeline change (in progress): vector config changes and clickhouse table migration. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/88
4) Dashboard implementation (in progress): create tileboard panels in console dashboard repo and wire trace links. Draft board: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/obs/callgraph-tileboard
5) Rollout: canary to 10% of requests for two weeks, monitor cost delta and sampling fidelity, then global rollout.

Rollout gating and risk mitigation:
- Canary only at trace-sampling route-level; default sampling remains unchanged until we validate cost.
- Provide a dashboard that shows index size and ingestion rate (observability-cost panel) to guard against runaway metrics volume.
- If clickhouse indices or retention would exceed budget, fall back to 1-in-N aggregated telemetry and enable adaptive sampling.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Eng lead: Liam O'Connor
- PM: Sofia Martinez
- Design: Marco Chen (dashboard UX)
- Oncall/SRE reviewers: Priya Rao

Notes on tradeoffs considered:
- Full-fidelity per-token timing vs aggregated node histograms: chose histograms to avoid per-token flood while preserving percentile accuracy at tail.
- Inline trace tags vs synthetic correlation key: emitting both for compatibility; correlation key used for low-cardinality dashboards, tags used for trace drilldown.

Next steps:
- Finish infra PRs and coordinate with infra team for clickhouse migration (blocked on infra windows).
- Implement dashboard widgets and get design sign-off (UX review scheduled 2026-03-08).
- Create alerting playbook and runbook for p99 regression responders.
